messages:
marie: Heads-up: during QA I noticed the metric tiles grid at narrow widths (<=240px) shows y-axis labels like `requests.p95_count` wrapping to two lines. This causes row heights to vary and the grid looks jittery. Proposals: 1) compact stub: show tokenized labels (`p95`) + unit on one line and expand to full label on focus; 2) ellipsize with tooltip; 3) always show abbreviated keys with a legend elsewhere. Which do you prefer?

sam: I vote for the compact stub. Ellipses + tooltip is fine, but expansion on hover is bad for keyboard users unless we provide an explicit focus affordance.

alex: Compact stub + explicit expand control (small chevron or focus target) works. For the abbreviated visual, use `p95` and the unit `cnt` or `ms` on the same line. Keep the legend minimal: one-line legend entries, not long paragraphs.

toni: Accessibility: if you abbreviate visually, include full semantics in aria-labels. Example aria-label: "95th percentile requests (p95) in count". The expand control must be keyboard operable and announce state changes (e.g., "expanded: full metric name"). Also avoid relying on color for anything meaningful.

marie: Noted. I'll mock a left-stub with a 24px focusable area that toggles expansion via Enter/Space. For screen readers the stub will have aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing to the full label element.

sam: Smoothing: do we want per-tile toggles or a global on/off? I think per-tile is more flexible but we should have a global preference to avoid surprise. Implementation note: client-side smoothing with a stable kernel is easiest (3-sample median or exponential with fixed alpha).

alex: Agree. Microcopy suggestion for the control: label the toggle `Smoothing (reduce noise)` and tooltip text: `Use smoothing to emphasize trends. Turn off to see raw values and spikes.` Keep it short.

toni: Tooltip + aria-describedby linking to the same string ensures screen readers get the same explanation. For the legend icon for smoothing use a small wave icon and the text `smoothing`.

marie: Outliers: current approach dims extremes; that feels like hiding. Suggest showing a distinct marker (diamond) for anomalies, plus a legend entry like "◇ anomaly — deviates from baseline". Offer a toggle `Highlight anomalies` which also populates an adjacent anomalies table.

sam: Good. When `Highlight anomalies` is off, keep dimming subtle so users still see context. When on, markers should be focusable with aria-labels giving brief context: e.g., `Anomaly: 2025-04-02 03:00, 820 reqs (~4x baseline)`.

toni: Also provide a machine-readable data view via a table link labeled `View anomalies (text)` so screen-reader users can consume the full list. Provide keyboard shortcut hints in the tooltip if useful.

ui-bot: Preview link: https://staging.redwood.ai/preview/tiles/compact-stub (expires in 24h)

marie: Action items: (1) I will upload mocks for stub/expanded states + legend variants; (2) alex/sam, can you confirm the smoothing algorithm and perf constraints for client-side calc? (3) toni, I'll DM example aria strings for review including exact SR output. Will post mocks in ~2h. :thumbsup:
